subject: crowbar
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: crowbar, in the place of the game's models/v_crowbar.mdl, models/p_crowbar.mdl, models/w_crowbar.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_shotgun.mdl, models/w_9mmar.mdl, models/w_357.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked B, C, C, A where the asset was D, B, C, B: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The silhouette reads as a crowbar: a long straight bar with a bent claw at one end and a flared, flat wedge at the other, in sides.png (left, right, top, below and the diagonal views). The brief asks only for a red steel crowbar, so nothing in the outline contradicts it.

M2.reason: Measured 31.8 long against the brief's 32 (0.7% off), within 15%. Width 2 and height 7.2 are as built; the brief gives no other size.

M3.reason: The brief names a steel crowbar, a red grip and bare-metal tips, and no other parts. All are there: the hooked claw at one end and the flat wedge at the other, both on grey bare-metal tips, with the red grip between them (sides.png, lineup.png). No small part is missing. The shaft's cross-section cannot be counted from these views, and the brief does not ask for a count.

M4.reason: Red paint on the grip and grey bare steel on both ends, as the brief says. The grip's darker red bands are shading on one paint colour. In the first-person view the claw reads darker, but that is lighting on the same steel.

M5.reason: The brief's wear, bare metal at the tips, is there: a clean grey-on-red change at both ends, sharp in the sides and in-hand views. The shaft shows two red tones (a darker band in LEFT and RIGHT), which is shading, not a fault. Nothing the brief asks for is absent.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric. In the line-up test the asset was picked only once in four readings, so it passed for one of the game's.

M7.reason: The brief gives no facing. The model lies flat, thin in Z (2 units), with its length on the ground, which is how a world weapon rests. Nothing contradicts that. Front and back silhouettes are alike, so no front is visibly wrong.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. The asset has 60 triangles, well under twice the median of 142 for Half-Life's kind of this size. The visible ends and the grip show no open or floating faces.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the weapon sits where the game's own does, with the claw at the top left, the same way round and at the same angle. In attack.png the swing carries it out of the picture (frames 1, 2, 5, 8), which the rubric does not count as leaving the hands. The hands are not drawn in these pictures, so the grip is judged by the match to the game's own.
